references.text: The continuation of the account where God tells Gideon that he will use the 300 men who lapped water to save Israel
The preceding verse describing God's command to separate those who lap water with their tongue from those who kneel down to drink
The context in which God reduces Gideon's army to show that victory comes from the Lord, not from human strength
Jonathan's words that nothing can prevent the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few, reflect the same principle as Gideon's 300 men
Isaiah's prophecy about a remnant that will return, parallel to the small group God chose among Gideon's men
Paul teaches that God chooses what is weak in the world to shame what is strong, the same principle as when God chose 300 men
